Energy levels get closer together at higher energy.
Lyman: falls to n = 1, UV. Balmer: falls to n = 2, visible.

front: Electrons in s, p, d, f sublevels?

back: Fill lowest energy first; singly with parallel spins before pairing; max two per orbital with opposite spins.
Cr [Ar]3d⁵4s¹; Cu [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹.

front: Which electrons do transition metals lose first?
back: 4s before 3d.
Electron from n = ∞; its energy equals the ionisation energy.

front: (HL) What does a big jump in successive IEs show?
back: The next electron is in an inner shell; electrons before the jump = valence electrons.
Continuous: all wavelengths (white light). Line: only specific frequencies — evidence that electron energy levels are quantised.
E = hν and c = νλ, so E = hc/λ. Higher frequency (shorter λ) → higher energy.

front: Order of IR, visible and UV by energy?
back: IR < visible < UV in energy and frequency; wavelength decreases in the same order.

front: Shapes of s and p orbitals?
back: s: spherical. p: dumbbell-shaped, three per level (pₓ, p_y, p_z) at 90° to each other.
A region of space around the nucleus where there is a high probability of finding an electron; holds at most two electrons of opposite spin.

front: Filling order of sublevels up to 4p?
back: 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p — 4s fills before 3d because it is lower in energy in the neutral atom.
Fe: [Ar]3d⁶4s². Fe³⁺: [Ar]3d⁵ (both 4s electrons lost first, then one 3d).
1s ↑↓, 2s ↑↓, 2p ↑ ↑ ↑ — three unpaired electrons in separate 2p orbitals (Hund’s rule).

front: How do s, p, d, f blocks relate to configuration?
back: The block is the sublevel holding the highest-energy (outermost) electron: groups 1–2 s, 13–18 p, 3–12 d, lanthanoids/actinoids f.
Minimum energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms in their ground state: X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

front: (HL) Ionisation energy of H from the convergence limit?
back: Find the frequency (or wavelength) of the Lyman limit; E = hν per atom; × Nₐ, ÷ 1000 → kJ mol⁻¹ (≈ 1312 kJ mol⁻¹).

front: (HL) Why do successive IEs always increase?
back: Each electron is removed from an increasingly positive ion, so the remaining electrons are held more strongly (less repulsion, same nuclear charge).
Absorption: dark lines on a continuous background (electrons absorb photons and jump up). Emission: coloured lines on black (electrons fall and emit).

front: Do electrons pair up in a p sublevel as soon as possible?
back: No. Hund’s rule: they occupy each degenerate orbital singly with parallel spins before pairing (pairing costs repulsion energy).
